## Engagement in Employment, Education, or Training

### Entire Population

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Engagement in employment, education, or training - entire population, by LGA
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
engaged_lga <- f_read_census_lga("Aboriginal_Employment_Engagement_LGA.csv",
                                 variable = "engagement") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(!engagement %in% c("Engagement status undetermined/not stated", "Not applicable"))

# Data wrangling
engaged_lga <- engaged_lga %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(engagement = dplyr::case_when(
    engagement == "Fully engaged"              ~ "Fully engaged",
    engagement == "Partially engaged"          ~ "Partially engaged",
    engagement == "At least partially engaged" ~ "Partially engaged",
    engagement == "Not engaged"                ~ "Not engaged",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_)) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_lga(variable = engagement,
                       level    = "person",
                       dichot   = "no") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(fully_prop     = aboriginal_n_fully_engaged / aboriginal_total * 100,
                partially_prop = aboriginal_n_partially_engaged / aboriginal_total * 100,
                not_prop       = aboriginal_n_not_engaged / aboriginal_total * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(lga_name,
                fully_n = aboriginal_n_fully_engaged,
                fully_prop,
                partially_n = aboriginal_n_partially_engaged,
                partially_prop,
                not_n = aboriginal_n_not_engaged,
                not_prop,
                aboriginal_total)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Engagement in employment, education, or training - entire population, by age and sex
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
engaged_agesex <- f_read_census_agesex("Aboriginal_Employment_Engagement_AgeSex.csv",
                                       variable = "engagement") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(!engagement %in% c("Engagement status undetermined/not stated", "Not applicable"))

# Data wrangling
engaged_agesex <- engaged_agesex %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(engagement = dplyr::case_when(
    engagement == "Fully engaged"              ~ "Fully engaged",
    engagement == "Partially engaged"          ~ "Partially engaged",
    engagement == "At least partially engaged" ~ "Partially engaged",
    engagement == "Not engaged"                ~ "Not engaged",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_)) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_agesex(variable = engagement,
                          dichot   = "no") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(aboriginal_total = aboriginal_n_fully_engaged + aboriginal_n_partially_engaged + aboriginal_n_not_engaged,
                fully_prop       = aboriginal_n_fully_engaged / aboriginal_total * 100,
                partially_prop   = aboriginal_n_partially_engaged / aboriginal_total * 100,
                not_prop         = aboriginal_n_not_engaged / aboriginal_total * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~replace(., is.na(.), 0)),
                across(where(is.numeric), ~replace(., is.nan(.), 0))) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(age_group,
                sex,
                fully_n = aboriginal_n_fully_engaged,
                fully_prop,
                partially_n = aboriginal_n_partially_engaged,
                partially_prop,
                not_n = aboriginal_n_not_engaged,
                not_prop,
                aboriginal_total)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census).

- Overall, 52% (n = 4,334) of people living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census were fully engaged in employment, education, or training and a further 19% (n = 1,590) were partially engaged.

- The number of people who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who were fully engaged in employment, education, or training ranged from 724 (Whittlesea LGA) to 125 (Nillumbik LGA).

- The percentage of people who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who were fully engaged in employment, education, or training ranged from 63% (Boroondara LGA) to 49% (Darebin LGA).

- Younger people were more likely to be fully or partially engaged in employment, education, or training. Males were more likely to be fully engaged and females were more likely to be partially engaged.

::: {.callout-tip title="Census questions and definitions for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
The following questions were asked of all people aged 15 years and over completing the ABS Census 2021. Responses were cross tabulated to determine the type of engagement in work and/or study (fully engaged, partially engaged, at least partially engaged, not engaged) for each respondent.

- Is the person attending a school or any other education institution?
  - No
  - Yes, full-time student
  - Yes, part-time student

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- Last week, did the person have a job of any kind?
  - Yes, worked for payment or profit
  - Yes, but absent on holidays, on paid leave, on strike, or temporarily stood down
  - Yes, unpaid work in a family business
  - Yes, other unpaid work
  - No, did not have a job

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- Last week, how many hours did the person work in all jobs?
  - Free text response

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- Did the person actively look for work at any time in the last four weeks?
  - No, did not look for work
  - Yes, looked for full-time work
  - Yes, looked for part-time work

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- If the person had found a job, could they have started work last week?
  - Yes, could have started work last week
  - No, already had a job to go to
  - No, temporarily ill or injured
  - No, other reason

:::

### Young Adults

::: {.ctg-box}
**This topic aligns with [Closing the Gap Outcome Area 7](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/dashboard/outcome-area/youth-engagement/): Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander youth are engaged in employment or education**

Target: By 2031, increase the proportion of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander youth (aged 15-24 years) who are in employment, education, or training to 67%.
:::

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Engagement in employment, education, or training - trend over time
# Data from ABS Census via CtG Information Repository
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in ABS data
fully_trend <- f_read_ctg_indigenous("CTG07_Employment_Education_Data_Tables.xlsx",
                                      data_sheet     = "Table CtG7A.1",
                                      column_select  = c(indigenous_status = "x3",
                                                         year = "x4",
                                                         "vic",
                                                         "unit"),
                                      fill_variables = vars(indigenous_status, year),
                                      row_select     = 1:20)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Engagement in employment, education, or training - young adults
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data wrangling
fully_youth <- f_read_census_agesex("Aboriginal_Employment_Engagement_YoungAdult.csv",
                                    variable = "engagement") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(!engagement %in% c("Engagement status undetermined/not stated", "Not applicable")) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(engagement = dplyr::case_when(
    engagement == "Fully engaged" ~ "yes",
    TRUE ~ "no"))

# Data wrangling - by LGA
fully_youth_lga <- fully_youth %>% 
  f_wrangle_census_lga(variable = engagement,
                       level    = "person",
                       dichot   = "yes")

# Data wrangling - by age and sex
fully_youth_sex <- fully_youth %>%
  f_wrangle_census_agesex(variable = engagement,
                          dichot   = "yes") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(age_group == "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::bind_rows(fully_youth_lga %>% 
                     dplyr::filter(lga_name == "NEPHU") %>% 
                     #
                     dplyr::mutate(age_group = "NEPHU",
                                   sex       = "NEPHU") %>% 
                     #
                     dplyr::select(-lga_name))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Engagement in employment, education, or training - by age
# Data from ABS Census via CtG Information Repository
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in ABS data
fully_age <- f_read_ctg_indigenous("CTG07_Employment_Education_Data_Tables.xlsx",
                                   data_sheet     = "Table CtG7A.3",
                                   column_select  = c(indigenous_status = "x2",
                                                      year = "x3",
                                                      age = "x4",
                                                      "vic",
                                                      "unit"),
                                   fill_variables = vars(indigenous_status, year),
                                   row_select     = 1:80) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(year == "2021") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(age = stringr::str_replace(age, "years old", "yrs"))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [Closing the Gap Information Repository](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/), compiled from the ABS Census for the Census years between 2001 and 2021, as well as the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census).

- The percentage of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people aged 15-24 years living in Victoria who were fully engaged in education, employment, or training increased from 60% in 2001 to 66% in 2021.

- Overall, 70% (n = 1,555) of people aged 15-24 years living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census were fully engaged in education, employment, or training. This was lower than for non-Indigenous people living in the NEPHU catchment (82%).

- The number of people aged 15-24 years living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who were fully engaged in education, employment, or training ranged from 243 (Whittlesea LGA) to 36 (Manningham LGA).

- The gap between the observed number of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people aged 15-24 years who were fully engaged in education, employment, or training and the expected number if the proportion was the same as for non-Indigenous people was biggest for Whittlesea and Hume LGAs.

- The percentage of people aged 15-24 years living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who were fully engaged in education, employment, or training ranged from 100% (Nillumbik LGA) to 63% (Hume LGA).

- The Closing the Gap target (67%) has been met in 9 out of 12 LGAs in the NEPHU catchment. However, except for Yarra Ranges, these LGAs contained a small number of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people, with more populous LGAs such as Darebin, Hume, and Whittlesea not quite meeting the target.

- 72% (n = 819) of males aged 15-24 years living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census were fully engaged in education, employment, or training, compared to 68% (n = 736) of females.

- For people in the 15-24 year age group, the percentage of people fully engaged in education, employment, or training decreased with increasing age for both Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander and non-Indigenous people.

- Further historical and ongoing target context can be found on the [Closing the Gap Information Repository](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/dashboard/outcome-area/youth-engagement/).

**Key points from stakeholder consultation**

- At stakeholder consultation for this report, these data were discussed as being good evidence that counters stereotypes and stigma regarding Aboriginal youth employment.

- Given the improvement seen in youth engagement in education, employment, or training over time, it was also discussed whether the Closing the Gap target should now be higher.

## Employment

### Entire Population

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Employment - entire population, by LGA
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
status_lga <- f_read_census_lga("Aboriginal_Employment_Status_LGA.csv",
                                variable = "status") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(!status %in% c("Not stated", "Not applicable"))

# Data wrangling
status_lga <- status_lga %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(status = dplyr::case_when(
    status == "Employed, worked full-time"             ~ "Full-time",
    status == "Employed, worked part-time"             ~ "Part-time",
    status == "Employed, away from work"               ~ "On leave",
    status == "Unemployed, looking for full-time work" ~ "Unemployed",
    status == "Unemployed, looking for part-time work" ~ "Unemployed",
    status == "Not in the labour force"                ~ "Unemployed",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_)) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_lga(variable = status,
                       level    = "person",
                       dichot   = "no") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(full_prop  = aboriginal_n_full_time / aboriginal_total * 100,
                part_prop  = aboriginal_n_part_time / aboriginal_total * 100,
                leave_prop = aboriginal_n_on_leave / aboriginal_total * 100,
                not_prop   = aboriginal_n_unemployed / aboriginal_total * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(lga_name,
                full_n = aboriginal_n_full_time,
                full_prop,
                part_n = aboriginal_n_part_time,
                part_prop,
                leave_n = aboriginal_n_on_leave,
                leave_prop,
                not_n = aboriginal_n_unemployed,
                not_prop,
                aboriginal_total)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Employment - entire population, by age and sex
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
status_agesex <- f_read_census_agesex("Aboriginal_Employment_Status_AgeSex.csv",
                                      variable = "status") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(!status %in% c("Not stated", "Not applicable"))

# Data wrangling
status_agesex <- status_agesex %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(status = dplyr::case_when(
    status == "Employed, worked full-time"             ~ "Full-time",
    status == "Employed, worked part-time"             ~ "Part-time",
    status == "Employed, away from work"               ~ "On leave",
    status == "Unemployed, looking for full-time work" ~ "Unemployed",
    status == "Unemployed, looking for part-time work" ~ "Unemployed",
    status == "Not in the labour force"                ~ "Unemployed",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_)) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_agesex(variable = status,
                          dichot   = "no") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(aboriginal_total = aboriginal_n_full_time + aboriginal_n_part_time + aboriginal_n_on_leave + aboriginal_n_unemployed,
                full_prop        = aboriginal_n_full_time / aboriginal_total * 100,
                part_prop        = aboriginal_n_part_time / aboriginal_total * 100,
                leave_prop       = aboriginal_n_on_leave / aboriginal_total * 100,
                not_prop         = aboriginal_n_unemployed / aboriginal_total * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~replace(., is.na(.), 0)),
                across(where(is.numeric), ~replace(., is.nan(.), 0))) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(age_group,
                sex,
                full_n = aboriginal_n_full_time,
                full_prop,
                part_n = aboriginal_n_part_time,
                part_prop,
                leave_n = aboriginal_n_on_leave,
                leave_prop,
                not_n = aboriginal_n_unemployed,
                not_prop,
                aboriginal_total)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census).

- Overall, 36% (n = 2,970) of people living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census were employed full-time, 19% (n = 1,599) were employed part-time, 5.2% (n = 435) were on leave from work, and 40% (n = 3,355) were unemployed. Unemployed people includes both people who are not part of the labour force and those who were actively looking for work.

- This was similar to non-Indigenous people living in the NEPHU catchment (38% employed full-time, 22% employed part-time, 4.0% on leave from work, and 37% unemployed).

- Younger people were more likely to be employed (full-time, part-time, or on leave).

- Males were more likely to be employed full-time than females.

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
The following questions were asked of all people aged 15 years and over completing the ABS Census 2021. Responses were cross tabulated to determine the labour force status (employed full-time, employed part-time, employed but away from work, unemployed but looking for work, not in the labour force) for each respondent.

- Last week, did the person have a job of any kind?
  - Yes, worked for payment or profit
  - Yes, but absent on holidays, on paid leave, on strike, or temporarily stood down
  - Yes, unpaid work in a family business
  - Yes, other unpaid work
  - No, did not have a job

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- In the main job held last week, was the person:
  - Working for an employer
  - Working in own business

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- Last week, how many hours did the person work in all jobs?
  - Free text response

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- Did the person actively look for work at any time in the last four weeks?
  - No, did not look for work
  - Yes, looked for full-time work
  - Yes, looked for part-time work

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- If the person had found a job, could they have started work last week?
  - Yes, could have started work last week
  - No, already had a job to go to
  - No, temporarily ill or injured
  - No, other reason

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

- Employed people are defined as those who were employed full-time (35 hours or more per week), part-time (less than 35 hours per week), or on leave from work in the week prior to Census night.

- Unemployed people are defined as people who were not currently employed and were actively looking for work (either part-time or full-time) or people who were not part of the labour force.

### Working Age Adults

::: {.ctg-box}
**This topic aligns with [Closing the Gap Outcome Area 8](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/dashboard/outcome-area/economic-participation/): Strong economic participation and development of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people and communities**

Target: By 2031, increase the proportion of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people aged 25-64 years who are employed to 62%.
:::

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Employment - trend over time
# Data from ABS Census via CtG Information Repository
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in ABS data
status_trend <- f_read_ctg_indigenous("CTG08_Economic_Participation_Data_Tables.xlsx",
                                      data_sheet     = "Table CtG8A.1",
                                      column_select  = c(indigenous_status = "x3",
                                                         year = "x4",
                                                         "vic",
                                                         "unit"),
                                      fill_variables = vars(indigenous_status, year),
                                      row_select     = 1:28)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Employment - working age adults
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data wrangling
status_working <- f_read_census_agesex("Aboriginal_Employment_Status_WorkingAge.csv",
                                       variable = "status") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(!status %in% c("Not stated", "Not applicable")) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(status = dplyr::case_when(
    status == "Employed, worked full-time" ~ "yes",
    status == "Employed, worked part-time" ~ "yes",
    status == "Employed, away from work"   ~ "yes",
    #
    TRUE ~ "no"))

# Data wrangling - by LGA
status_working_lga <- status_working %>% 
  f_wrangle_census_lga(variable = status,
                       level    = "person",
                       dichot   = "yes")

# Data wrangling - by age and sex
status_working_sex <- status_working %>%
  f_wrangle_census_agesex(variable = status,
                          dichot   = "yes") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(age_group == "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::bind_rows(status_working_lga %>% 
                     dplyr::filter(lga_name == "NEPHU") %>%
                     #
                     dplyr::mutate(age_group = "NEPHU",
                                   sex       = "NEPHU") %>% 
                     #
                     dplyr::select(-lga_name))

```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [Closing the Gap Information Repository](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/), compiled from the ABS Census for the Census years between 2001 and 2021, as well as the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census).

- The percentage of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people aged 25-64 years living in Victoria who were employed (full-time, part-time, or on leave) increased from 52% in 1991 to 62% in 2021.

- Overall, 69% (n = 3,453) of people aged 25-64 years living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census were employed (full-time, part-time, or on leave). This was lower than for non-Indigenous people living in the NEPHU catchment (79%).

- The number of people aged 25-64 years who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who were employed (full-time, part-time, or on leave) ranged from 604 (Whittlesea LGA) to 66 (Manningham LGA).

- The gap between Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander and non-Indigenous people was biggest for Darebin and Yarra Ranges LGAs.

- The percentage of people aged 25-64 years who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who were employed (full-time, part-time, or on leave) ranged from 82% (Boroondara LGA) to 65% (Maroondah LGA).

- All 12 LGAs in the NEPHU catchment were above the Closing the Gap target of 62%.

- 66% (n = 1,661) of females living in the NEPHU catchment aged 25-64 years who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census were employed (full-time, part-time, or on leave), compared to 73% (n = 1,792) of males.

- Employed people are defined as those who were employed full-time (35 hours or more per week), part-time (less than 35 hours per week), or on leave from work in the week prior to Census night.

- Unemployed people are defined as people who were not currently employed and were actively looking for work (either part-time or full-time) or people who were not part of the labour force.

## Volunteer Work

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Volunteer work, by LGA
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
volunteer_lga <- f_read_census_lga("Aboriginal_Employment_Volunteer_LGA.csv",
                                   variable = "volunteer") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(!volunteer %in% c("Not stated", "Not applicable"))
  
# Data wrangling
volunteer_lga <- volunteer_lga %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(volunteer = dplyr::case_when(
    volunteer == "Volunteer" ~ "yes",
    TRUE ~ "no")) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_lga(variable = volunteer,
                       level    = "person",
                       dichot   = "yes")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Volunteer work, by age and sex
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
volunteer_agesex <- f_read_census_agesex("Aboriginal_Employment_Volunteer_AgeSex.csv",
                                         variable = "volunteer") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(!volunteer %in% c("Not stated", "Not applicable"))

# Data wrangling
volunteer_agesex <- volunteer_agesex %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(volunteer = dplyr::case_when(
    volunteer == "Volunteer" ~ "yes",
    TRUE ~ "no")) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_agesex(variable = volunteer,
                          dichot   = "yes")
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census).

- Overall, 14% (n = 1,154) of people living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census did volunteer work for an organisation or group. This was similar to non-Indigenous people living in the NEPHU catchment (14%).

- The number of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who did volunteer work for an organisation or group ranged from 193 (Yarra Ranges LGA) to 34 (Nillumbik LGA).

- The gap between Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander and non-Indigenous people was biggest for Whittlesea and Hume LGAs.

- The percentage of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who did volunteer work for an organisation or group ranged from 22% (Yarra LGA) to 9.3% (Hume LGA).

**Key points from stakeholder consultation**

- Consultation feedback during the development of this report emphasised that these data are unlikely to be an underestimate.

- It was discussed that many Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people do not see helping out in their community as volunteering activity, but rather something that is just done.

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
The following question was asked of all people aged 15 years and over completing the ABS Census 2021.

- In the last 12 months did the person spend any time doing unpaid voluntary work for an organisation or group?
  - No, did not do any voluntary work
  - Yes, did voluntary work

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

## Unpaid Carers

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Unpaid carers - entire population, by LGA
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
carer_lga <- f_read_census_lga("Aboriginal_Employment_Carer_LGA.csv",
                               variable = "carer") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(!carer %in% c("Not stated", "Not applicable"))

# Data wrangling
carer_lga <- carer_lga %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(carer = dplyr::case_when(
    carer == "Provided unpaid assistance" ~ "yes",
    TRUE ~ "no")) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_lga(variable = carer,
                       level    = "person",
                       dichot   = "yes")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Unpaid carers - entire population, by age and sex
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
carer_agesex <- f_read_census_agesex("Aboriginal_Employment_Carer_AgeSex.csv",
                                     variable = "carer") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(!carer %in% c("Not stated", "Not applicable"))

# Data wrangling
carer_agesex <- carer_agesex %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(carer = dplyr::case_when(
    carer == "Provided unpaid assistance" ~ "yes",
    #
    TRUE ~ "no")) %>% 
  
  f_wrangle_census_agesex(variable = carer,
                          dichot   = "yes")
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census).

- Overall, 17% (n = 1,430) of people living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census undertook unpaid caring duties. This was higher than for non-Indigenous people living in the NEPHU catchment (14%).

- The number of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who undertook unpaid caring duties ranged from 233 (Hume LGA) to 35 (Manningham LGA).

- The gap between Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander and non-Indigenous people was biggest for Hume, Knox, and Whittlesea LGAs.

- The percentage of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who undertook unpaid caring duties ranged from 22% (Whitehorse LGA) to 13% (Yarra LGA).

- Females were more likely to undertake unpaid caring duties compared to males.

**Key points from stakeholder consultation**

- The Aboriginal kinship system is a cultural strength of communities and often creates a network of people who have caring responsibilities.

- Individuals may not be defining themselves as ‘carers’ despite undertaking unpaid caring duties for family or other community members. This could lead to an underestimate of the number of unpaid carers.

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
The following question was asked of all people aged 15 years and over completing the ABS Census 2021.

- In the last two weeks did the person spend time providing unpaid care, help, or assistance to family members or others because of a disability, a long-term health condition, or problems related to old age?
  - No, did not provide unpaid care, help, or assistance
  - Yes, provided unpaid care, help, or assistance

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::
